title: Money and shopping
cando: understand prices and amounts, and buy things in a shop or market

about.text: In this lesson you go to a market and buy fruit and vegetables. You ask the prices, choose what you want and pay. Then you read a price list and a receipt. You check your change.
goals: Ask and understand prices: How much are these apples?
Say numbers to 1,000 and prices: two hundred and fifty, four pounds seventy.
Choose things with this, that, these and those: That one, please. The big one.
Read a price list and a till receipt, and write a shopping list.
Buy three things at a stall and check the receipt.

chapters.title: At the market
chapters.text:
In this lesson you buy food at a market.
At a market, people sell fruit and vegetables at a stall.
First, you ask the price. How much are these apples? How much is this bag?
Then you ask for what you want. Can I have a kilo, please?
To choose one thing, you can point and say: That one, please. The big one.
Listen carefully to the numbers. Thirteen and thirty sound close.
If you are not sure, ask: Sorry, thirteen or thirty?

chapters.title: Numbers, prices and this or that
chapters.text:
Now, numbers up to a thousand.
After hundred, say and. Two hundred and fifty. Three hundred and twenty-five.
Say a price like this: four pounds seventy, or just four seventy.
For pence, people often say p. Eighty p is eighty pence.
Next, this, that, these and those.
This and these are near you. That and those are not near you.
This bag, these apples. That bag, those apples.
You don't need to say the thing again. Say one or ones. The big one. The green ones.

chapters.title: A price list and a receipt
chapters.text:
Next, you read a price list and a receipt from a market stall.
The price list shows the price for a kilo, or for one thing.
The receipt shows what you bought, the total and your change.
Look at the receipt and the price list together. Is every price the same?
Then you write your own shopping list, with an amount for every thing.

chapters.title: Buy and check
chapters.text:
Then you buy three things at a stall.
Ask the prices, and say how much you want.
Ask for a receipt, and check it before you go.
Is something not right? Say it politely: Sorry, I think there's a mistake.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story about money and shopping.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again and answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: Where do you usually buy fruit and vegetables?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Markets are often cheap, and you can choose every apple yourself. But you must listen carefully to the prices.

conversation.title: At the fruit and vegetable stall
conversation.setting: It is Saturday morning. Tomasz is at the market. He wants fruit and vegetables for the week.
lines: Hello. How much are these apples?
The red ones are two pounds a kilo. The green ones are one pound fifty.
Can I have a kilo of the green ones, please?
Yes. How much are the oranges?
OK. Four oranges, please. And a bag of potatoes.
No, that one, please. The big one.
That's two pounds. So that's four pounds seventy, please.
Thanks. Here's your change: thirty p. Have a nice day!

questions.q: How much is a kilo of the green apples?
questions.why: The stallholder says: The green ones are one pound fifty.
Tomasz checks the number. The stallholder says: Thirty. Three, zero.
The stallholder says: So that's four pounds seventy, please.

sound.title: thirteen or thirty
sound.explain: These numbers sound close. In thirteen, the end is strong and long: thir-TEEN. In thirty, the start is strong and the end is short: THIR-ty. Listen, then say each group.
lines: The oranges are thirty p each.

sayIt.instructions: Say Tomasz's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Are your numbers clear?
lines: Hello. How much are these apples?
Can I have a kilo of the green ones, please?
No, that one, please. The big one.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. Some point at things. Some give a price.
examples: The green ones are one pound fifty.
No, that one, please. The big one.
So that's four pounds seventy, please.
spot.question: Which words point at things? Which word means you don't say apples or bag again? How do you say a price?
spot.answer: These apples: near Tomasz, more than one. That one: not near him, one thing. One and ones: the big one is the big bag. The green ones are the green apples. A price: pounds, then pence: four pounds seventy.

rules.title: Numbers to 1,000 and prices
rule: After hundred, say and: 150 is a hundred and fifty. 325 is three hundred and twenty-five.
No s after a number: two hundred, not two hundreds. 1,000 is a thousand.
£4.70 is four pounds seventy, or four seventy.
80p is eighty p, or eighty pence. £1 is a pound.
500 g is five hundred grams, or half a kilo.
rules.mistake: Not: two hundred fifty. Say: two hundred and fifty.

rules.title: This, that, these, those, and the red one
rule: Near you: this for one thing, these for two or more: this bag, these apples.
Not near you: that for one thing, those for two or more: that bag, those apples.
Don't say the thing again. Say one or ones: the big one, the green ones.
Ask: Which one? Which ones? Answer: That one, please. The red ones.
rules.mistake: Not: this apples. Say: these apples.

yourTurn.prompt: You are at a market stall. Ask two prices, then ask for three things. Use this, that, these or those, and one or ones.
yourTurn.model: How much are these tomatoes? And how much is that bag of potatoes? Can I have half a kilo of the red tomatoes, please? And six bananas. And that bag of potatoes, please. The big one.

text.title: Stall 12: prices and a receipt
text.body:
PRACTICE: this stall and this receipt are not real.

RIVERSIDE MARKET · STALL 12
Fresh fruit and vegetables

TODAY'S PRICES
Apples: £1.80 a kilo
Bananas: 20p each
Tomatoes: £3.00 a kilo
Carrots: 80p a kilo
Onions: 90p a kilo
Potatoes: £2.00 a bag
Apple juice: £2.50 a litre
Pay at the till. Cash or card.

RECEIPT
Riverside Market · Stall 12
Saturday 14 June, 10:25
Apples, 1 kg: £1.80
Tomatoes, 500 g: £1.50
Bananas, 6 at 25p: £1.50
Apple juice, 1 litre: £2.50
TOTAL: £7.30
Cash: £10.00
Change: £2.70

Thank you! Please keep your receipt.

gist.q: What are the two parts of this text?
gist.a: a price list and a receipt
wrong: a shopping list and a note
gist.why: The first part is TODAY'S PRICES. The second part is the RECEIPT.
The sign says: Fresh fruit and vegetables.

detail.q: How much is half a kilo of tomatoes?
detail.why: A kilo is £3.00, so half a kilo is £1.50.

detail.q: Which price on the receipt is different from the price list?
detail.why: The price list says 20p each, but the receipt says 25p.

detail.q: How much should six bananas cost?

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher has a stall. Buy three things, pay, and check your receipt. Then change roles: you sell, and your partner buys.
doIt.wehel: You sell fruit and vegetables at a market stall. I want to buy three things. Tell me the prices. Say one price with thirteen, fifteen or sixteen, so I must check it. At the end, tell me the total and give me my change. Make one small mistake in the total, so I can find it. Use simple English.

model.title: At the stall
lines: Hello! What can I get you?
Hello. How much are the carrots?
A kilo, please. And half a kilo of those tomatoes.
The red ones? They're three pounds a kilo.
Yes, please. And that bag of potatoes. How much is it?
No, thanks. Can I have a receipt, please?
Of course. That's five pounds eighty.
Thanks. Here's your change and your receipt.
Sorry, the receipt says one kilo of tomatoes. I've only got half a kilo.
Oh, you're right. Sorry! Here's one pound fifty back.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the market conversation in pairs. Then change the fruit, the vegetables and the prices, and check the numbers: thirteen or thirty?
Day 2: numbers race. Say a price or a weight, and the others write it. Then point at things in the room: How much is this one? How much are those?
Day 3: the stall. You sell; each learner buys three things and checks the receipt. Put one mistake on each receipt.
Day 4: talk about the book, answer questions, and let two learners read their shopping lists aloud.
